name: User Timing marks and measures
plain: Lets a page stamp named points in time and measure the gaps between them.
meaning: A site can time its own code in detail and send the numbers home, so it learns how fast the person's device and network really are. The marks live only in this tab and are not shared across sites.

access.persistence: Per page; entries are in memory until the page closes or clearMarks is called
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Per frame; Timing is same-origin only for the page's own entries
steps: Browser records a timestamp with sub millisecond precision (subject to coarsening)
Page reads entries or sends them to a server

limits.headline: Can mark points in time and measure gaps between them inside the page
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens as the page runs
can: Stamp named moments in its own code
Measure how long each part took
Send the timings home to the site
Learn how fast your device and network really are
cannot: Share marks between tabs, since they live in this tab only
Keep the marks after you close the tab

story.what_it_is: A page can mark named points in time and measure the gaps between them.

marketing.name: User Timing
marketing.pitch: Lets developers add their own timing marks, so they can measure how long key steps take.

story.for_you: You never see it. Teams use it to label steps like Search started and Results shown, then measure from real visitors. That is how they find what slows you down.
story.for_makers: It is the standard way to time what matters to your product, such as time to first video frame or time to checkout. Teams send the results to dashboards to compare releases.

use_cases.example: A shop marks Add to cart clicked and Cart updated, then watches the gap by device.
A video site marks play pressed and first frame shown to measure start up time.
A game portal times the gap between game page load and the first playable frame.
A web editor times how long a file takes to open and become editable.
A monitoring tool collects all custom marks and charts them by release.
A web map times how long the first map tiles take to show after a search.
A booking site times from Search to first results, to watch speed on slow phones.

technical_bounds: Entries are per document and are not shared across origins
Timer resolution is coarsened: Chrome uses 100 microseconds (5 microseconds on cross-origin isolated pages); Firefox rounds more coarsely by default
No hard entry limit in the spec; browsers hold them in memory until cleared
detail object lets a page attach arbitrary data to a mark
